title: TSB contract fixture file
description: The format of every file under fixtures/C1..C8/. A fixture is the record of one contract clause: consumers read it, providers prove it. `grade` says how `tsbc verify` grades it against a provider: `live` runs it against a URL; `artifacts:<check>` runs the named check over a `--artifacts` directory; `with:<fixture>` takes the result of that fixture, whose run validates real instances of this fixture's shape; `reference` means only a provider's own test can grade it, and `graded_by` names that test in prose; the index `fixtures/graded-by.json` (graded-by.schema.json) names it again, in the form a run can check, and a run grades such a fixture only when that test passed in the results it was given.

mark.description: At least one key. required-green: the provider must pass it from this epoch on. published: surfaces may build against it from this epoch.

graded_by.description: For a reference fixture that is required green: the provider tests that grade it, by unit and path, in prose. The form a run checks is fixtures/graded-by.json; this key stays the fixture's own description of who grades it.

description.description: What the fixture proves and why it matters.

corpus.description: The clauses this fixture encodes, cited by document and section.

input.description: Run-time inputs a live fixture needs; README 'Inputs' names the environment variable for each. Credentials are never written into a fixture.

pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON pointer into a response body or frame.

saves.description: Variable name → pointer; the value is saved for later steps as ${name}.

ignore.description: Opt-in exclusion of this top-level response field from both objects before equality comparison.

oneOf.description: The array at pointer has an element where every sub-pointer in `some` equals its value.
The array at pointer has no element where every sub-pointer in `none` equals its value.
No listed string may appear anywhere in the JSON serialization of the whole response, including keys and nested values (Unicode is not ASCII-escaped).

cleanup.description: Requests run after the steps whatever their outcome, so a fixture leaves no session behind.

as.description: Whose cookie: main (the run's login, the default), peer (a second principal), fresh (this fixture's own jar, empty at its first step), none.

invalid_body.description: The body breaks the request schema on purpose (a 422 case). Self-check then requires that it does NOT validate.

keep_cookies.description: Ignore Set-Cookie on this response, so the next request still presents the cookie held before it. Proves logout invalidates the session on the server, not only in the client.

match.description: Each pointer reads the response body. For GET /alerts' 200, whose body is an event stream, it reads the list of the alert events' data, in the order they arrived (index 0 first).

example.description: A concrete body of the kind this step expects. Self-check validates it against the operation's response schema; consumer tests may decode it strictly.

headers.description: Named response headers whose values must match exactly. For GET /sessions/{id}/output's 200 this names TSB-Page-* headers. A null value means the response MUST NOT carry that header.

binary_body.description: For a response whose body is application/octet-stream: the body's length and content, rather than a JSON shape.

poll.description: Repeat the request until the expectation holds or the run's timeout expires.

unknown.description: The frame's `t` is deliberately not in the schema (the receiver must ignore it).

invalid.description: The frame deliberately breaks the schema.

bytes.description: Sent as one binary frame: the UTF-8 encoding of this string after ${} substitution.

oneOf.description: The attach prefix: the text frame, then one binary message that contains or lacks given strings. The text frame is matched first; the binary message is the dump.

match.description: Each pointer reads the prefix text frame.

binary_contains.description: Each string must appear in the binary dump message.

binary_lacks.description: Each string must not appear in the binary dump message.

wait.description: Seconds to sleep before the next step, or a ${placeholder} saved from a response (a ticket's expires_in, say). The runner refuses more than 120.

unknown.description: The message names a cmd or event this tag does not define, on purpose (the receiver's rule for unknown messages is under test).

run.description: The core run the message belongs to, as a capture line carries it (artifacts-collected.schema.json run): a sequence that spans a core restart marks each message's run.

invalid.description: The message breaks its sender's schema on purpose (a receiver's rule for a malformed line is under test). Self-check then requires that it does NOT validate.

file.description: A sibling file holding the exact bytes; it is the ground truth.

sidecar.description: For a C8 recording: the sibling file holding its sidecar.

max_message_bytes.description: For C4 frames: the maximum message size (a contract range, R7) the .bin was encoded under, so a chunked blob is graded against the same value the codec chunks at.

messages.description: For C4 frames: the decoded messages, in stream order.

invalid.description: For a C8 recording: recordings a reader must refuse, as the exact bytes of both files, each with the problem it must be refused for.

runs.description: For C3 frames across core restarts: one tap per run, in run order, as a run-bounded collection holds them (artifacts-collected.schema.json run-frames).

input.description: c3-to-c8: the tapped frames (`file` or `frames`), and `end` {end_state, timestamp} when the session ended; from contract-v0.2 also `handshakes` (the hello_ack numbers each gap frame's marker is computed from), `committed` {out_bytes, last_out_ts, last_seq, created_at} (what the recording held before these frames, and where a span starts when it held no output yet) and `end.spool` {last_seq, out_bytes, last_out_ts} (a spooled end's numbers). c5-rediscovery: supervisors, workers and sockets. c5-rediscovery-v0.2: the same, plus `spool` (spool entries) and `audited` (session ids the core has already audited). c8-compare: two recordings of one session, `a` and `b`, each as `frames`. The four inventory transforms: `reads`, a list of inventory-tree states, each {current: the link's target or null, index_before: the entries the reader keeps when current is missing, root_files: names in the inventory root, files: {source, name} with the file's parsed `doc` (the JSON form) or its `yaml` tree — a scalar as {text: the scalar's text, yaml11: string|int|float|bool|null|timestamp}, which is what a YAML 1.1 reader sees}; the output is `results`, one {index, alerts, docs} per read, as the reader rule gives them.
